threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'do you want a cup of tea' instead of 'fancy a cuppa?' while awkwardly holding a latte.
Last night on the 196, a guy took his pet parrot for a ride. The parrot started squawking every time we hit a bump. Everyone loved it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy feeding pigeons seeds while casually balancing a coffee cup on his head at the Gesperrte Straße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that serves beer-fueled karaoke alongside a wall painted with street art from local kids. Totally unique vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local by the way they seamlessly navigate the BART delays. Tourists just stand there confused while we roll our eyes and check our phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo catch the 38 Geary at 4 AM, clearly coming from a wedding. The Muni never sleeps, and neither do the party-goers.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about hip cafés, but the best spots are those little bodegas with locals arguing over the football match.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion at the ‘tancat’ signs on Carrer de Verdi; they still think it’s a suggestion, not a rule.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their confused face at the London Fields park's entrance - it's not 'picnic', it's 'pint and chill' now.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week. A guy was silently eating a full roast from a takeaway box. The smell? A mix of gravy and exhaust!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy fixing his bike while balancing a falafel plate on his knee, all while chatting with the neighborhood cat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a hidden bookshop that doubles as a bar where locals sip cocktails while browsing dusty tomes. It’s the cozy chaos of Kreuzberg.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they roll their eyes when someone asks about the BART delays. It's like a rite of passage here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy juggling on the Muni bus while the driver fumbled with the fare machine. Only in the Tenderloin, right? Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume all the locals love the bustling Plaça del Sol, but most of us avoid it after dark—too loud, too wild.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still ask locals for directions to Parc Güell instead of Googling it.
